Hamilton parcel geometry has no key, so the spine key is minted from the geometry. NPCA ARN parcels, address points and buildings attach to it, and the City Boundary is the clip mask.

Hamilton publishes no shared parcel ID. The only ID joins are by ARN, which exists on 36% of the city through the NPCA pull (MPAC itself, plus 23 HCA managed-forest rows), and by address string between two address sets.
Most of the work is in Tier 2 and Tier 4.
Spatial overlays attach almost all parcel context. The registers attach by address, through the address points linked to the spine.
59 of its 133 rows are StatCan Business Counts releases at CMA/CSD level. The rest are City dashboard tables by year or ward, and census polygons.

Steps 1 to 16 are the spine track and run in order. Steps 17 to 25 are the nature and context track. That track depends only on the City Boundary, so it can run in parallel from the start, for example as a separate an agent batch.

Pull every P1 layer clipped to the City Boundary.
Most are under 2k features. The big ones are parcels (166,828), addresses (274,725), buildings (214,292), existing land use (22,391) and zoning (11,860).
Parcels and NPCA ARN are already local on deb.
Attach the NPCA ARN by reciprocal representative point. Attach addresses by point-in-polygon, and buildings by largest overlap.
Output one parcels table carrying: key, grain, community, ARN where present, address list and building count.
This is the only stage that needs an agent-grade care.

Employment Lands, Urban Boundary and Rural Settlements: centroid flags.

Take the % of each parcel inside the HCA and NPCA regulated areas.

The City has an uncatalogued existing-land-use layer.
has 22,391 polygons and was last edited 2024-04. Its
classes are Industrial, Warehousing, Vacant Lands, Commercial, Office and others. Until an Official Plan layer exists, it is the strongest open "what is this land used for" signal, so it is P1.
Conservation authority coverage is now mapped.
the City publishes one dissolved polygon per CA (HCA, Conservation Halton, NPCA, GRCA), so every parcel can name its regulator (A07).
limits are reachable only through a Region of Waterloo proxy service, with 188 polygons tagged City of Hamilton (A10).
no open regulation layer was found (A11).
The nature layers were marked not relevant.
Parks (633 polygons), Trails (3,437) and HCA Trails sit in
. The "encased by nature" view needs at least Parks.
The city has its own copy of the provincial wetlands.
has 2,693 polygons, cleaner than clipping the LIO layer.

LIO publishes the Greenbelt Outer Boundary, Specialty Crop, Towns/Villages and Hamlets, the NEP Boundary, Policy Areas and Minor Urban Centres, and the Natural Heritage System. None of these are catalogued for Hamilton.
Addresses expose no address ID; Cooling Towers'
So every Tier 4 join is an address-string match. Address normalisation is a shared prerequisite and is worth building once.
Owner-like fields need dropping at ingest under D-13:
on the Heritage Property Grant table, and councillor contact fields on Ward Boundaries.
"City encased by nature": layers that feed the first view
Greenbelt Outer Boundary (A12) and Greenbelt Designation (C363, 20 polygons in the Hamilton bbox).
Parks_OD (A04, re-admit), LIO Wooded Area (A22, 7,483 in bbox) and the Escarpment line (C145).
The regulated-area overlays: HCA (C255), NPCA (A09) and the CA areas (A07).

Natural Heritage System (A13), wetlands (A06), ESA (C134), ANSI (A21), HCA forest cover (C279), Trails (A05), Watercourse and Waterbodies (C130, C169), the provincial park (A23) and the GRCA and CH regulation limits (A10, A11).

most of the green ring sits outside the Urban Boundary. One way to get the encased look is to render Greenbelt, NEP and woodland at full opacity, and to dim or shade the area outside the Urban Boundary polygon (C164). Filed for INSIGHTS.md.
PR #61 lifted the MPAC/NPCA rule only for a password-protected site. On public GitHub Pages, do ARN and
ship in tiles, or are they used build-side only, for example to flag "assessed as industrial" without the roll number? This blocks the Stage F tiles, not the spine.

Is a geometry hash, such as a quantised representative point plus area, acceptable as the Hamilton parcel key, NA-83-style? How should it survive City refreshes, given the layer is tagged "Temp" and was last edited 2024-12-20?
Do you accept the reciprocal representative-point join (99.6%) as the NPCA-to-City link and log the IoU offset (p50 0.88) as a separate task? Or should the offset be measured and corrected first?
For the parcels outside NPCA's watershed: render refusals (
), ask the City for an ARN-attributed parcel layer, or get an MPAC/Propertyline quote?
and lean on Employment Lands plus Existing Land Use as clearly labelled proxies? Or should someone digitise UHOP E-1 / RHOP D, or request the layer from the City?
Request the regulation limit from CH, or ship CH-area parcels with a named refusal? And is the GRCA layer through the Region of Waterloo proxy acceptable as the source?
Existing Land Use has a "Vacant Lands" class and there is a Vacant Building Registry. The PCDP forbids "vacant/available" claims. Are these OK if shown as a quoted source class with its authority?
Should the 27 web-check rows (A01 to A27) and the 3 proposed re-admits go into catalog 09 and the MCS? That needs a commit. Separately, are the
layers superseded and safe to ignore?
Display-only Tier 3 for v0, or claimed
on each parcel (a cheap overlay) from day one?
Show the dominant zone only, or every zone touching the parcel with area shares? The latter is more honest but needs more UI space.

Tables with an address field go to Tier 4. Tables with only year, ward or total fields go to Tier 5.
Ward, census tract and FSA polygons go to Tier 5.

Other points and polygons go to Tier 2, with manual overrides for about 90 named datasets.
Generic rows have role and join text like "point layer" or "polygon overlay". Treat those as defaults, not reviewed judgements.
City and HCA counts are whole-layer counts, since those layers are Hamilton-scoped.
LIO counts are envelope intersections of the City bounding box (-80.252, 43.049, -79.617, 43.472). They overcount slightly, because the box catches Burlington, Grimsby and west Lincoln.
The catalog's counts for Addresses (273,535) and Buildings (214,293) differ slightly from today's live counts (274,725 and 214,292).
